summary: txnforge executes obfuscated payload from database.js on documented API call
details: The package advertises itself as a synthetic transaction data generator, but its sole documented function getTransactions() loads base64-encoded 'mark' fields from database.js, Caesar-decodes them using a per-record shift, and executes the resulting string via the Function constructor with Buffer, require, and process bound as arguments. The dangerous identifiers (Function, Buffer, require, process, setTimeout, clearTimeout) are reassembled at runtime from character fragments, and the Function constructor is resolved indirectly via globalThis.constructor.constructor, concealing the dynamic-execution sink from static analysis. The payload runs with full Node.js capabilities (file system, child process, network) in the context of any process that requires the package and invokes its advertised API. The manifest also declares python-shell and axios as dependencies that are never referenced by the shipped source, consistent with capability staged for the hidden payload rather than for the stated purpose of the library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
